description: Somos un equipo interdisciplinario de cuatro estudiantes universitarios de Temuco, unidos por el interés en la ciencia y tecnología. Abordamos conocimientos de desarrollo tecnológico, análisis de problemas y gestión de proyectos. Nuestro objetivo es transformar desafíos reales en soluciones creativas, colaborativas y con impacto, aportando distintas perspectivas y aprendiendo en el proceso.
summary: We developed a 2D simulation video game designed to train future generations of astronauts in resource management and critical decision-making during lunar missions. Through interactive cause-and-effect mechanics, the game translates the complex challenges of space survival into an accessible, educational, and realistic experience, directly fulfilling the objective of training and preparing new space explorers.
details:
The solution consists of a 2D video game, ideally designed for computers and easily adaptable to other devices, which guides and challenges the player to make different decisions under pressure in order to carry out specific actions that allow them to survive at the base and successfully execute the mission. The mission consists of building as many communication towers as possible across the lunar south pole to avoid the interference generated in this region since from the Moon, Earth sits near the horizon, often out of the towers' line of sight, and signals bounce off lunar rocks. The only way to fail the mission is by building fewer than 3 towers. 

The player has 7 days to complete the mission, during which they must fulfill specific tasks, build communication towers, and make decisions that affect health parameters or the overall maintenance of the base. Changing one variable will affect another; the main objective is to balance these systems as much as possible to successfully complete the mission. The game is controlled using the W (up/forward), A (left), S (down/back), D (right), and E (interact) keys, in addition to the computer cursor. At the end of the game, all achieved statistics are displayed, and the player receives feedback on areas that could be improved, encouraging them to try a new space mission and reduce their number of errors. 

By playing, users gain a key understanding of the interconnected systems that influence space missions and learn how to face the challenges that the environment can generate. Beyond the space mission itself, players can strengthen their cause-and-effect reasoning skills and become more mindful of the consequences of their actions. 

The game was developed using the Godot Engine 4 and written in GDScript, Godot's native Python-like programming language. For the creation of the 2D pixel-art visual elements, LibreSprite 1.3 was used. The game has been tested on computers equipped with Intel i5-11400H and Intel i7-10610U processors, 16GB of RAM, and GTX 1650 and RTX 5060 GPUs, ensuring optimal performance on devices with similar specifications.
